01.r: Rehoboam sends his labour chief to the rebelling tribes.
01.n: The Hebrew puts the verb first: 'and sent the king Rehoboam'.

03.n: Gesenius: the name means 'who enlarges the people'; the son and successor of Solomon.

04.r: Marks Adoram as the one sent.
04.n: This small word marks a definite direct object and has no English equivalent; it is counted here with 'Adoram'.

05.r: The officer in charge of the labour gangs.
05.n: STEPBible's lexicon: an officer of David and of Rehoboam, also called Adoniram and Hadoram.

07.n: The Hebrew has only the preposition 'over'; 'was' is understood. Geneva makes him 'the receiuer of the tribute', a collector of money.

08.r: The drafted labour that the tribes had complained of.
08.n: BDB: a body of forced labourers, formed by levy upon the people. The ASV's 'the men subject to taskwork' and the BSB's 'the forced labor' follow that sense; the KJV, Geneva, DRC and YLT say 'the tribute', the sense Gesenius gives.

09.r: The crowd kills him by throwing stones.
09.n: Gesenius gives the root sense as to heap up, and so to pile up stones, to cast stones, to stone. The Hebrew puts the verb first: 'and stoned him all Israel'.

10.r: The whole assembly of the northern tribes.

11.r: Here the tribes who rejected Rehoboam.

12.n: Literally 'on him' or 'at him', the preposition this verb takes.

13.n: Singular in Hebrew, 'stone', used collectively; Gesenius notes this collective use.

15.r: The scene turns back to Rehoboam.

16.r: The king, now in danger himself.

17.r: He acts quickly and with effort to get away.
17.n: Gesenius: to be alert, firm, strong, properly of alertness of the feet; the brief's lexicon gives for this form 'to be determined, to make oneself alert'. YLT renders the form literally, 'hath strengthened himself'; most versions give the sense, 'made speed'.

19.r: His chariot, the means of escape.
19.n: Gesenius: a chariot, especially a war chariot. The Hebrew says 'the chariot'; most versions say 'his'.

21.n: The Hebrew has the bare name; 'to' is understood from the verb of motion.

01.n: ἀποστέλλω, to send out, the root of 'apostle'.

02.n: The Greek has only 'the king' here; Rehoboam's name first appears later in the verse.

05.n: Swete reads Ἀράμ, a short form of the name; the brief's matched dictionary form (Adoniram) is loose.

06.n: τὸν, 'the one': 'the one over the tribute'.

08.n: φόρος, tribute: the Greek, like the KJV, makes Adoram a collector of tribute, where BDB reads the Hebrew as forced labour.

09.n: λιθοβολέω, to throw stones at. The Greek does not have 'all Israel'.

17.n: φθάνω, to come first, to be beforehand: he was quick to get away.

18.n: The Greek does not mention the chariot.

20.n: φυγεῖν is from φεύγω, to flee; the brief leaves its dictionary form blank.
